p71.002: The state is a useful fruit that civilization has gained as it evolved. The Urantia Book says the state is society's net gain from the pain of war. The state is not a sacred institution that came down from heaven, and it was not planned and built by anyone. It is a product of evolution that arose on its own through the long struggles in which groups tested their strength against one another.
p71.004: The state is an organization that governs society on the basis of a certain territory. The strongest and longest-lasting states are made up of a single people with the same language, customs, and institutions. Early states were small, and all of them came about through conquest. The northern tribes of the American red men had good government, but they lacked things such as private property, cities and agriculture, clear territory, and strong leaders, so they never grew into true states. Rome, on the other hand, succeeded on the basis of agriculture and cities, roads and territory, and strong rulers.
p71.005: But Rome too fell in the end. The Urantia Book says that Rome's fall shows what happens to a nation that weakens on the inside while growing too fast on the outside. The state came about as clans bound by blood gave way to communities bound by land. When a state fails to hold together, it can slip back into an old pattern of breaking up into small castles, like the feudal system of medieval Europe.
p71.007: The Urantia Book says that democracy is an ideal, but it did not simply evolve on its own; it is an achievement of civilization. So it advises, “⟦Q 71:2.1⟧Go slowly! select carefully!⟦/Q⟧” Democracy carries dangers, such as praising mediocrity, choosing ignorant leaders, and being dragged along by public opinion. The majority is not always right. That is why educating public opinion is the safest way to move civilization forward. The Urantia Book says that the more bullets are replaced by ballots, the faster culture grows. Elections do not always make the right decision, but they are a way of doing even a wrong thing in the right way.
p71.008: There are ten steps on the way to representative government: freedom of the person, freedom of the mind gained through education, the rule of law instead of the whims of people, freedom of speech, security of property, the right of petition, the right to take part in ruling, universal suffrage in which everyone votes, the power to oversee public servants, and choosing well-trained, moral representatives. Only when these conditions are in place can government of the people, by the people, and for the people be preserved.
p71.010: The Urantia Book says that what a government does matters more than what form it takes. A good government is one that gives its citizens liberty, security, education, and harmony. No state can rise above the moral level of its citizens, and ignorance and selfishness will bring down even the finest government. Also, no state can reach its ideal until every kind of intolerance has disappeared. Intolerance is best overcome through science, commerce, play, and religion.
p71.011: The ideal state is moved by love that comes from understanding that people are brothers, by wise patriotism, and by a broad cosmic outlook. Such a nation has few laws, its people govern themselves, and they use their growing leisure in worthwhile ways. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 71:3.9⟧That state is best which co-ordinates most while governing least.⟦/Q⟧” In an advanced nation, the wisest and noblest citizens serve their country and regard public office as the highest honor.
p71.013: Economics, society, and government must keep evolving if they are to survive. Standing still means falling behind. A progressing civilization seeks personal liberty, the protection of the home, economic security, the prevention of disease, education, worthwhile leisure, care for unfortunate neighbors, the advancement of science, art, and wisdom, and spiritual insight. All of these finally lead to the highest goals: a society where all people are brothers, and individuals who know God.
p71.014: A true brotherhood is a society in which everyone gladly bears one another's burdens and practices the golden rule. But as long as there are people who want to take advantage of the good, even a peace-loving society must be ready to defend itself. The Urantia Book says that this is the great test of idealism: can a nation have the power to defend itself and yet not use that power to attack others? Only love and brotherhood can keep the strong from oppressing the weak.
p71.016: Competition is necessary for society to progress, but competition without rules breeds violence. Today competition is more and more taking the place of war. The ideal state regulates society just enough to prevent violence and unfairness in competition. In the early days of civilization, competition stirs people up, but the more civilization advances, the more efficient cooperation becomes compared to competition. The Urantia Book says that even attempts to get rid of the waste of competition must not take away the basic liberties of the individual.
p71.018: The Urantia Book says that an economy that chases only profit will collapse in the end unless it grows into a desire to serve. Ruthless competition based on narrow selfishness destroys even the very things it was meant to protect. In economics, the relationship between profit and service is like the relationship between fear and love in religion. But the desire for profit should not be wiped out all at once, because it is a force that makes many people hardworking. It must change slowly until people come to have higher motives, such as wisdom, brotherhood, and spiritual achievement.
p71.020: A lasting state stands on culture, is guided by ideals, and has service as its motive. The purpose of education is to gain skill, to seek wisdom, to realize oneself, and to reach spiritual values. In an ideal nation, education continues all through life, and philosophy, the love of wisdom, becomes the citizens' most important study. The Urantia Book says that education must move away from looking only at the local area and chasing only success, and become an education that sees the world and understands the universe.
p71.021: Education is a lifelong task, and it climbs up through several levels. It starts with knowing things, then grows into understanding meanings, recognizing values, knowing the nobility and duty of work, setting moral goals, building a character that loves service, and finally reaching spiritual discernment. Along this path, many people will rise all the way to the level of God-consciousness.
p71.023: The Urantia Book says that the only sacred feature of human government is the division of power into three parts: executive, legislative, and judicial. The universe too is governed by dividing power this way. As long as this is kept, it does not matter much what form of state people choose, so long as the citizens are moving toward governing themselves and serving society.
p71.024: A state develops through many stages: the separation of the three powers, social, political, and religious freedom, the ending of all forms of slavery, the citizens' power to control taxes, lifelong education, the progress of science and the conquest of disease, the equality of men and women in the home, school, church, and society, a world language, the end of war through international courts, and an age when the whole world loves wisdom. The Urantia Book says that Urantia is still far from this ideal, but that humankind has begun to walk toward a higher destiny. When each of us becomes a citizen who learns and serves, those steps will grow faster.
p72.002: This paper is very special, because it describes the society and government of a neighboring planet in the same system of Satania as our Earth. It is very rare for the affairs of one planet to be told to another. That planet's history is the most like Urantia's. Its Planetary Prince also joined the Lucifer rebellion, its Material Son also failed, and it was cut off from the universe circuits. What is more, unlike Urantia, it has never received a bestowal Son from Paradise.
p72.004: In spite of these difficulties, a very advanced civilization is growing on one continent of that planet, about the size of Australia. It has about 140 million people, and several races are mixed together and live in harmony like brothers. The average length of life is ninety years. In the middle of the nation are high mountains with plenty of rain, which are good for water power and for watering the land. The nation can provide for its own needs, but because its less advanced neighbors are hostile, it has almost no foreign trade.
p72.005: This nation also went through an age of tribes, an age of kings, and an age of failed republics and dictators. About five hundred years ago, one of three dictators had a change of heart and stepped down on his own, and the nation was united. After that, under a strong king, a fine charter of liberty grew up, and the king's power slowly weakened until it disappeared. The present republic has lasted for two hundred years.
p72.007: This nation is a federation of one hundred states. State governors and state lawmakers serve ten-year terms and cannot be elected again. No city may have more than one million people. The federal government is divided into three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial. The chief executive is elected every six years by the vote of all the people, and the living former chief executives advise him.
p72.008: The legislature has three houses. The upper house is elected according to the kind of work people do, such as industry and the professions, and the lower house is elected according to social, political, and philosophical groups. The third house is made up of one hundred elder statesmen who have served the nation for a long time; it only gives advice, but it has great influence on public opinion. Besides the regular courts, there are also parental courts that deal with family matters, educational courts that deal with school matters, and industrial courts that deal with economic disputes.
p72.010: In this nation, two families are not allowed to live under one roof, and each home is given plenty of land. Both fathers and mothers must attend parental schools to learn how to raise children. The average family has five children. Taking in a child who has lost its parents is considered a great honor, and such children are placed with the families that show the best parenting qualities. Fathers give just as much care to their children's education as mothers do.
p72.011: These people consider the home the foundation of civilization. Sex education and religious education are given at home by the parents. For them, religion means striving to know God, serving their neighbors, and showing love. No one may marry before age twenty, and to marry, a couple must announce it a year ahead and finish the training of the parental schools. The rules for divorce are not very strict, yet the divorce rate is only one tenth of that in the civilized nations of Urantia.
p72.013: From age five to eighteen, all boys and girls go to school together. But these schools have no classrooms, and students study only one subject at a time. After the first three years, every student becomes an assistant who teaches younger students. Books are used as references when solving problems that come up in the school workshops and on the school farms. A quarter of school time is spent on athletics and play, and there are contests in public speaking, music, science, and philosophy.
p72.014: The main aim of education in this nation is to raise every student as a citizen who can stand on his or her own feet. So every student who graduates at eighteen is a skilled worker. After that, students do serious book study and learn specialized knowledge in college. One month of each year is a vacation for traveling with family, and this too is part of lifelong education.
p72.016: Industry in this nation is still far from ideal, but it is moving toward capital and labor cooperating with each other. Workers are more and more becoming shareholders of their companies. When slavery was abolished a little over a hundred years ago, it was done slowly, by freeing a certain number each year, so there was no great upheaval. Settling disputes by violence is forbidden, and industrial disputes are decided in the industrial courts. Income is first divided into interest on capital, salaries for managers, and fair wages for workers, and the profit left over is shared equally among the three.
p72.017: People work six hours a day, four days in a row, and then rest one day. Two hundred years ago the desire for profit ruled industry, but now it is changing to higher motives. Competition is still keen, but people compete in play, skill, science, intellectual achievement, and social service. Even the richest person on this continent, after working six hours a day, goes to study at the school of statesmanship in order to hold public office. People think laziness and income they did not work for are shameful.
p72.019: Instead of charity that hurts people's self-respect, this nation tries to care for the old and the sick with dignified old-age insurance. This is possible because it gives education to every child and work to every person. People retire at sixty-five. The pensions come from things like everyone paying in one day's earnings each month, estates left by the wealthy, and income from the nation's natural resources. These funds have been managed honestly for a long time, and betraying the public trust is considered the most serious crime.
p72.021: The federal government directly handles only old-age pensions and the fostering of genius, while the cities take care of matters of daily life, such as health, sanitation, water supply, recreation, and music. Cities may not collect taxes or go into debt, and the federal government may not go into debt either. In no year may a tax of more than one percent of a property's value be charged, and there is no tax on home sites. The federal government pays its way with duties on imported goods, half the profits from inventions and creative works, inheritance taxes, income from renting out military equipment, and income from natural resources.
p72.023: Besides basic education, there are special schools. The most important is the school of statesmanship, which teaches how to govern the nation. To hold public office, a person must graduate from this school, and the higher the position, the higher the grade of school that must be completed. There are also schools of philosophy, institutions of science, schools for the various professions, and military schools.
p72.025: Every candidate for public office must be a graduate of the school of statesmanship. All men and women over twenty have the right to vote, and they vote not according to where they live but according to the work they do and the groups they belong to. The Urantia Book explains that this nation uses a system that gives extra votes, up to ten per person, to people who have served society greatly or who pay large taxes. But in electing the chief executive, everyone has exactly one vote. Voting is a duty, and people who fail to vote pay heavy fines.
p72.027: The Urantia Book itself says that some of the ways this nation deals with crime look good, but others would shock most people on Urantia. The Urantia Book explains that this nation applies the death penalty to serious crimes and that justice is carried out surely and swiftly. They are moving from laws that punish to laws that prevent crime ahead of time, and the murder rate on this continent is only one percent of that in the other nations.
p72.029: This nation keeps a strong army to guard against attacks from its hostile neighbors. Yet for more than a hundred years it has not used that power to invade others. The Urantia Book praises them for being civilized enough to defend their civilization without giving in to the temptation to make war on others. Military training is always combined with training in a trade or profession, so no class of professional soldiers arises. In peacetime the military facilities are used for trade and recreation. And this nation puts far more effort into training statesmen, scientists, and philosophers than soldiers.
p72.031: This continental nation is ahead of the nations of Urantia in many ways, but the other continents of that planet are still far behind. Now, for the first time, a great religious leader has appeared in this nation and wants to send missionaries to the neighboring nations. The Urantia Book worries that they may make the mistake of forcing their own culture and religion on others. It says that it would be far better to bring the outstanding young people of the neighboring nations here, teach them, and send them back as ambassadors of culture, and asks what wonderful things might happen then.
p72.032: The Urantia Book also reminds us that Urantia is in better circumstances than that planet. Jesus came to Urantia, the Spirit of Truth has been poured out, and the differences between peoples here are not so great. So Urantia is much better prepared to move toward a world peace based on law and a true spiritual age. The story of our neighboring planet makes us look again at how great the gifts we have already received are, and what kind of world we can build with them.
p73.002: Caligastia's rebellion badly damaged people's culture and spiritual life, but the evolution of their bodies did not stop; it kept going. About forty thousand years ago, the Life Carriers who looked after life on the planet and the Melchizedek receivers decided that the time had come to send a Material Son and Daughter. The Urantia Book explains that a Material Son and Daughter are beings sent to lift up the bodies and minds of an evolving race by one step. In answer to their petition, a universe inspector examined the planet and recommended it, and in less than a hundred years Adam and Eve arrived.
p73.004: On a normal planet, the coming of a Material Son opens an age of great inventions and science, but this did not happen on Urantia. Ten thousand years after the rebellion, almost everything achieved in the days of the Prince had been lost. The culture of Dalamatia survived in only two groups. One was the Nodites, the descendants of the rebel staff, and the other was the Amadonites, the descendants of the people who stayed loyal to Van and Amadon.
p73.005: There was an old hatred between the two groups, so every time they tried to work together, quarrels broke out. After Dalamatia fell, the Nodites scattered toward the area near the Persian Gulf, the highlands of Elam, and the coast of Syria. Before Adam and Eve came, these two groups were the people with the most advanced culture in the world.
p73.007: For a long time Van and his associates had been preaching that the long-promised Son of God would come. Most people were not interested, but those who were close to Van took his words seriously. Van knew that the Material Sons on Jerusem always lived in simple and beautiful garden homes. So eighty-three years before Adam and Eve arrived, he proposed that they prepare a garden to welcome them.
p73.008: Van and Amadon gathered more than three thousand volunteers and divided them into one hundred companies. Caligastia and Daligastia did everything they could to interfere with the work, but thanks to the tireless help of nearly ten thousand loyal midway creatures, most of their interference was blocked.
p73.010: The committee searching for a site for the Garden looked all over for almost three years, and in the end it chose a peninsula, almost like an island, that reached westward from the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea. Thanks to the surrounding mountains, its climate stayed mild and even. It seldom rained in Eden, but each night, from the irrigation channels, a “⟦Q 73:3.3⟧mist would go up⟦/Q⟧” to refresh the plants. Four streams flowing from the hills of the peninsula joined into a great river that flowed eastward.
p73.011: The mountains around it were rich in gems and metals, but the people paid no attention to them. Their goal was to grow plants and to honor agriculture. The Urantia Book says that this was probably the most beautiful place in the whole world, and that in a world wrapped in darkness and ignorance, Eden was the only bright spot.
p73.013: The home of a Material Son is often called the Garden of Eden, because its flowers and plants are as beautiful as those of Edentia, the capital of the constellation. Van set aside the whole peninsula for the Garden, and his instructions were that “⟦Q 73:4.1⟧Eden was to be a garden, and only a garden⟦/Q⟧”. No animal was ever killed inside the Garden. First a brick wall was built across the narrow neck of the peninsula, and outside it another small wall was built, with wild animals let loose between the two walls as a line of defense.
p73.014: No paid workers took part in building the Garden; only volunteers did. When Van suggested that they also train the younger generation in case the Son and Daughter were late in coming, people thought he lacked faith and were disappointed, and many of them left. Still, Van did not waver; he kept on with the preparations and filled the places of those who had left with young volunteers.
p73.016: In the middle of the peninsula stood a stone temple dedicated to the Universal Father. To the north was the administrative headquarters, to the south the homes of the workers, to the west the site for the schools, and to the east the home of Adam and his family. When Adam arrived, the Garden was only one quarter finished, but it already had long irrigation channels, paved roads, more than five thousand brick buildings, and countless trees and plants.
p73.017: The sanitation of the Garden was more advanced than anywhere else on Urantia up to that time. The rules for keeping drinking water clean were strict, waste was carefully buried, and later covered sewers were built too. The Urantia Book says that the people of Urantia came to realize the importance of preventing disease again only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Many fruits and grains were improved there, and The Urantia Book says that Urantia has never, before or since, had such a beautiful garden.
p73.019: In the very center of the Garden temple, Van planted the tree of life that he had guarded for so long. The Urantia Book says that the “⟦Q 73:6.3⟧tree of the knowledge of good and evil⟦/Q⟧” may be a symbol, but that the tree of life was not a myth; it was real. This tree was a shrub sent from Edentia when Caligastia's staff came, and it held a special universe energy that held back aging. But its fruit worked only for beings with a special makeup; it was of no use to ordinary people. Van and Amadon, too, lived for more than one hundred and fifty thousand years thanks to this tree.
p73.020: Adam and Eve also ate its fruit to keep their bodies going. But after the plan failed, Adam's family was not able to take the tree with them. Later, the Nodites who invaded Eden ate the fruit, believing it would make them like gods, but it had no effect at all, and in their anger, after quarreling, they burned the temple and the tree. Now all the people of Urantia meet death in the natural way and afterward follow the universe path of waking up again on the mansion worlds.
p73.022: After Adam left, the first Garden was taken over by one group after another. Then, about four thousand years later, volcanic activity and movements of the earth caused the floor of the eastern Mediterranean to sink, and the whole Eden peninsula slowly went down under the sea over several hundred years. The Urantia Book states clearly that this was a natural event, not a failure of God's plan or a punishment for the mistakes of Adam and Eve.
p73.023: From the beginning, the Garden was never meant to be a permanent home for Adam's family. They had a mission to become messengers carrying new life to the whole world, and to give themselves freely for people in hard situations. Eden finally disappeared, but the devotion of Van and his people, who trusted the promise and quietly prepared for long years, teaches us, too, how precious it is to wait and to prepare.
p74.002: Adam and Eve arrived on Urantia 37,848 years before A.D. 1934, in the season when the Garden was in full bloom. Two seraphim carried them and landed near the Father's temple, and for ten days their bodies were remade to suit this planet. The two of them woke up at the same moment. A Material Son and Daughter always work together as a pair, and never being separated is the very heart of their service.
p74.004: Adam and Eve were one of the pairs of Material Sons and Daughters living on Jerusem, and they were more than eight feet tall. For more than fifteen thousand years they had been assigned to study the energies that change living things, and before that they had been teachers of newcomers. When volunteers were called for to go to Urantia, the entire corps of Material Sons and Daughters volunteered, and this couple was chosen from among them.
p74.005: The two of them had stayed loyal to Michael during the Lucifer rebellion. They were told in detail about Urantia's difficult situation, and they were also advised to follow the guidance of the Melchizedek receivers. Leaving behind fifty sons and fifty daughters on Jerusem, they set out with the blessings of many.
p74.007: The first to greet Adam and Eve when they woke were Van and Amadon. The language of Eden was the Andonic tongue that Amadon spoke, and Van and Amadon had polished this language by creating a new alphabet of twenty-four letters. Adam and Eve had already learned the language. Carrier pigeons flew in every direction to spread the news, and great crowds of people came flocking to Eden on pilgrimage.
p74.008: At the welcoming ceremony held on a hill, the Melchizedeks handed over the responsibility for ruling the planet to Adam and Eve, and Van laid down the authority he had held for more than one hundred and fifty thousand years. Then the voice of Gabriel announced that a new age had begun. In this way the age of Adam began, simple and yet majestic.
p74.009: 3. Adam and Eve Learn about the Planet
p74.010: After the installation ceremony, Adam and Eve felt painfully that this planet was cut off from the universe. The universe broadcasts they were used to could not be heard, and the fallen Prince Caligastia was still on the planet. On the first night, the two of them walked through the Garden under the full moon and, feeling lonely, talked over the future together. On the second day, they heard the detailed story of the rebellion and realized how foolish it is to try to rush progress while ignoring God's plan.
p74.011: On the third day, they rode a great bird and viewed the Garden from the sky, and on the fourth day they announced to the people their plans to rebuild the world. At this time women too were chosen for the new council of leaders, an amazing thing that had not happened since Dalamatia. On the fifth day they organized a temporary government, and on the sixth day they looked over the animals. Adam could know an animal's nature with only one look and gave it a fitting name, and the people were filled with wonder.
p74.013: On the night of the sixth day, while Adam and Eve were asleep, the people decided that the two were far too humble and, since they were no different from gods, they should be worshiped. Van opposed this, but it was no use, and the people even wanted to worship Van. Through the midway creatures, Van hurried to tell Adam the news.
p74.014: On the morning of the seventh day, Adam stood on a hill and said clearly that only God the Father may be worshiped. He said he could accept respect, but never worship. Then he told the people to go to the temple and worship the One who made us all. This was the beginning of the Sabbath tradition. In Eden, the seventh day became a day for caring for the body in the morning, the spirit at noon, and the mind in the afternoon, and for sharing joy together in the evening.
p74.016: About seven years later, the Melchizedek receivers returned to Jerusem, and Van and Amadon left this world along with them. For a while things went well. Adam widened trade with the tribes outside the Garden and set up more than a hundred small factories. The practice of sending ambassadors between tribes also began in Adam's time, and this was a big step in the development of government.
p74.017: But most of the world was not yet ready to accept Adam's culture. When Adam tried to extend his plans beyond the Garden, Caligastia and Daligastia worked against him unseen. Even inside Eden, people swayed by Caligastia's teaching of “⟦Q 74:5.6⟧unbridled personal liberty⟦/Q⟧” caused trouble. In the end, Adam set aside for a while his plan to set up representative government, and governed the people by dividing them into companies of one hundred, the way Van had done.
p74.018: 6. Home Life of Adam and Eve
p74.019: The firstborn son of Adam and Eve was Adamson. Eve bore sixty-three children before leaving the Garden, and by then the family had grown to more than sixteen hundred people over four generations. Adam's family did not cook; they ate fruits, nuts, and grains once a day. Light shone from the bodies of the two, but because it was covered by their clothing, only the light around their heads could be seen. The Urantia Book says that the halo painted around the heads of holy people came from this.
p74.020: Adam's children learned in their own schools until age sixteen, and older children taught younger ones. The sight of children playing happily just for the fun of it was something new on Urantia. The Urantia Book says that most of the play and humor of people today came from Adam's descendants. They loved music and had a keen sense of humor.
p74.022: The purpose of the schools on the west side of the Garden was to learn how to live together. In the morning students learned gardening and farming, in the afternoon games, and in the evening friendship with others. They also learned about health, the golden rule, the rights and duties of individuals and the community, the history of the different races, trade, and how to compete through play and humor instead of fighting. Teaching about religion and sex was the parents' job. The moral law of Eden was like the seven commandments of Dalamatia, but it also taught that the Thought Adjuster, the spirit of God, lives within each person, as one more reason not to harm life.
p74.023: Adam taught that prayer should not be a set text but the “⟦Q 74:7.21⟧desire of the soul⟦/Q⟧”, and he tried to have people offer the fruit of the land instead of blood sacrifices. He also taught that women contribute just as much as men to the making of new life, trying to plant the equality of the sexes. The Urantia Book explains that Adam's mission included a plan to lift humankind up by one step in both body and mind, and says that if this plan had worked out, Urantia would have become a very different world.
p74.025: The Urantia Book explains that the story of the world being created in six days came from the tradition that Adam and Eve spent six days on their first survey of the Garden. Setting apart the seventh day as a day of worship also came from what happened then. The story that Eve came from Adam's rib is said to have arisen when it got mixed up with an exchange of life material that took place much earlier, when the Prince's staff came. The Urantia Book says that even people of long ago knew that humankind had developed slowly.
p74.026: According to The Urantia Book, the creation story of the Old Testament was written down long after Moses, and it took shape after the Babylonian captivity by taking in stories from Mesopotamia. The Urantia Book says that the “⟦Q 74:8.14⟧golden age⟦/Q⟧” is a myth, but that Eden was a fact. Adam and Eve worked in the Garden for one hundred and seventeen years, but through the impatience of Eve and the errors of judgment of Adam, they turned aside from the appointed way. Even with a great purpose in mind, rushing can ruin the work: that is one of the lessons this story gives us.
p75.002: Adam worked hard on Urantia for more than a hundred years, but the world outside the Garden had hardly changed. Adam often wondered whether some special method, not in the original plan, might be needed, and he shared this thought with Eve many times. The two of them were faithful, but they were lonely, far from their own kind, and they were deeply troubled by the miserable state of the world.
p75.004: On Urantia, wounded and isolated by rebellion, Adam's mission was an enormously difficult task. The Urantia Book explains that on a normal planet a Material Son and Daughter first work at lifting up the bodies and minds of the human race, but on Urantia that work seemed almost hopeless. People's minds and morals were at a low level, even the simplest faith had to be taught from the beginning, and instead of one language, hundreds of dialects were jumbled together. The Urantia Book says that no Adam was ever placed on a more difficult world.
p75.005: After the Melchizedeks left, the loneliness of the two grew even greater, and their courage slowly weakened. The Urantia Book says that if they had looked a little farther ahead and been patient, they would have succeeded someday. But the two of them, especially Eve, were too impatient. They wanted to see results right away, and they did see results, but those results became a great disaster both for themselves and for the world.
p75.007: The fallen Prince Caligastia often came to the Garden and urged an easier way, but Adam and Eve firmly refused. They had clearly seen the results the rebellion had brought. Caligastia had no power to force anyone's will. So he gave up on Adam and decided to approach Eve cleverly, by making use of outstanding people among the Nodites.
p75.008: Before they left, the Melchizedeks had especially warned Eve never to leave her husband's side and never to try any method secretly on her own. For more than a hundred years Eve faithfully kept this advice. But she did not see the danger in her meetings with a Nodite leader named Serapatatia becoming more and more private and secret. Everything moved along so slowly and naturally that Eve was drawn in without realizing it.
p75.010: Serapatatia was the leader of the Syrian Nodites, and he was so deeply moved by Adam's purpose that he and his tribe lent their strength to the work of the Garden. He became one of Adam's most capable and honest assistants. The Urantia Book stresses again and again that he never knew he was being used by Caligastia, and that he was sincere in every proposal he made.
p75.011: While talking with Eve, Serapatatia came up with the idea that if the Nodites had a leader with Adam's bloodline, their people would be more firmly tied to the Garden. He too was impatient to see something happen right away. This plan ripened secretly for more than five years, and at last Eve met secretly with Cano, the spiritual leader of the Nodites. Swayed by praise, enthusiasm, and persuasion, Eve agreed to have a child by Cano, hoping to add her own small plan to God's great plan. Before she understood what was happening, a step that could not be undone had already been taken.
p75.013: The celestial beings were stirred up, and Adam sensed that something had gone wrong. Only then did he hear the whole story of the plan that had been ripening for so long. Then the seraphim who wrote this paper, called “⟦Q 75:4.2⟧the voice in the Garden⟦/Q⟧”, announced that they had broken the Garden covenant and disobeyed the instructions of the Melchizedeks. Every time they ate the fruit of the tree of life, they had been warned not to mix good and evil. Here, good means following God's plan, and evil means misapplying that plan so that it brings confusion.
p75.014: The Urantia Book says that even though this plan came from a sincere wish to help the world, it was evil, because it tried to reach a right goal by a wrong method and turned aside from God's plan. That night the seraphim gave Adam and Eve advice. The Urantia Book explains that the Bible story in which God calls out, “⟦Q 75:4.8⟧Where are you?⟦/Q⟧” tells of this very meeting.
p75.016: Eve was in deep despair, and Adam's heart was broken, but he felt nothing but pity for Eve. Then the next day, Adam deliberately made the same mistake Eve had made. He was not deceived; he knew exactly what he was doing. He loved his wife so much that he could not bear to be left alone without her, so he chose to share her fate.
p75.017: When the people of the Garden found out about this, they were furious; they attacked the nearby Nodite settlement and killed everyone, and Cano lost his life then too. Serapatatia could not overcome his fear and regret and took his own life. Adam wandered alone for thirty days, and during that time Eve and the children lived in great fear and sorrow. The Urantia Book says that innocent children often have to share in the results of their parents' foolishness. Soon the Nodites in the north gathered an army to take revenge, and a long and bitter struggle between the Adamites and the Nodites began.
p75.018: 6. Adam and Eve Leave the Garden
p75.019: When the Melchizedeks returned, they only told Adam to do whatever he himself thought best. Adam hated war, so he chose not to resist and decided to hand the first Garden over to the Nodites. With about twelve hundred loyal followers, he left Eden to look for a new home.
p75.020: On the third day after they left, seraphic transports came from Jerusem and gave the children a chance to choose. Of the children over twenty, two thirds chose to go to Edentia, and one third chose to stay with their parents. All the younger children left for Edentia. The two who had come with great hope and had been warmly welcomed now left Eden in shame, parting from more than three quarters of their children. The Urantia Book says that seeing this makes us realize how hard the way of the wrongdoer is.
p75.022: Gabriel appeared and announced the verdict. Adam and Eve were judged to have broken the trust they had been given as rulers of the planet. But they were cleared of the charge of rebelling against the universe government. They had not joined the rebellion. Instead, they were lowered to the same mortal status as the ordinary people of this planet, and from now on they had to live as a man and a woman of Urantia.
p75.023: The two of them had been warned many times, long before, that this would happen if they turned far aside from God's plan. Their immortality had been kept up by minds connected to the spiritual circuits of the universe and by the energy of the tree of life, but when they broke their trust, that connection was cut, and they could no longer reach the tree of life. The Urantia Book says that what they did was evil, but that it was not contempt for truth or knowing rebellion.
p75.025: Adam and Eve fell from their high position to the place of mortal humans, but The Urantia Book says clearly that this was not the “⟦Q 75:8.1⟧fall of man⟦/Q⟧”. The history of humankind is a history of evolution that moves forward little by little, and Adam's visit actually left humankind much better off than before. So Adam should not be thought of as the cause of a curse upon the human race. Although the plan failed, what they left behind helped a great deal in moving Urantia's civilization forward.
p75.026: The Urantia Book says that on the way to Paradise, nothing is gained by trying to get around God's plan with shortcuts or clever schemes of our own. Our universe was not created perfect; perfection is not our starting point but our eternal goal. The fact that mistakes and failures can happen is proof that the universe is not a machine but a place where personalities live and act. So The Urantia Book rejoices in how glorious this universe of growth and adventure is. Even when we have good intentions, the patience to walk the right path to the end without rushing matters: that is the lesson the story of Adam and Eve leaves us.
p76.002: When Adam decided to give up the first Garden to the Nodites without a fight, there were not many ways he and his followers could go. They had no boats to cross the sea to the west, the Nodites were invading from the north, and hostile tribes lived in the hills to the south. So they set out toward the east, the only way left open, heading for the pleasant land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. During this journey Cain and Sansa were born. Sansa's mother died giving birth to her, and Eve took Sansa into her arms and raised her along with her own son Cain. Sansa grew up to be a fine woman, married the leader of the blue people in the north, and helped her people make progress.
p76.004: It took Adam's caravan almost a year to reach the Euphrates River. The river was flooding, so they waited about six weeks before they could enter the land between the two rivers, the place that would become the second garden. The people who lived there were frightened by the news that the king of Eden was coming and fled to the hills, so when Adam arrived, the land was empty. The two rivers formed a natural line of defense, and by building a defensive wall where the rivers came close together, they could protect the land.
p76.005: But life here was completely different from life in the first Garden. The first Garden had been partly prepared for them, but the second had to be made by working the land with their own hands, in the “⟦Q 76:1.4⟧sweat of their faces⟦/Q⟧”. The Adamites had to live in primitive ways, struggling against harsh nature.
p76.007: Less than two years after Cain was born, Abel was born. Abel became a shepherd who kept sheep, and Cain became a farmer. At that time it was the custom to bring offerings to the priests from what one had produced, and the priests, who came from the Nodites, preferred animal offerings in the old way. Abel used this to mock his older brother, and he also kept bringing up the fact that Cain was not Adam's son. Cain had inherited a fighting nature from his Nodite father, and his hatred for his brother kept growing. At last, when they were eighteen and twenty, Cain, angered by Abel's taunts, killed Abel.
p76.008: This story shows how much influence environment and education have on character. Abel had inherited a fine heredity, but the bad surroundings of his early years nearly covered up that good foundation. The text says that a good social environment and proper education are the indispensable “⟦Q 76:2.6⟧soil and atmosphere⟦/Q⟧” for bringing out the best in a good inheritance.
p76.009: After that, Cain felt lonely and uneasy among people. In fear and regret, he went to his mother Eve and asked for spiritual help, and when he sincerely sought God's help, a Thought Adjuster (the spirit of God who lives within a person's mind) came to dwell in him. Cain went east to the land of Nod and became a fine leader of the tribe there, and all his life he worked for peace between the Nodites and the Adamites.
p76.011: Adam and Eve longed for the beautiful home they had lost, but they bore their lowered position with dignity and courage. Adam spent most of his time teaching his children and his associates. Because he had taught them how to govern, how to teach, and how to worship, the affairs of his people did not falter even after he died. The work of governing was carried on by Adam's son Eveson and Eveson's son Jansad, and the work of leading religion began with Seth, a son born in the second garden. The priests descended from Seth took on three jobs together: leading worship, serving as physicians who cared for the sick, and serving as teachers in the schools.
p76.012: The Adamites had brought many seeds and domestic animals from the first Garden, so they were far ahead of the surrounding tribes. They created the third alphabet, kept alive the skills of writing, metalworking, pottery, and weaving, and developed a style of building that no one could match for a long time. Unlike the money-seeking priests of later times, the Sethite priests were true educators with fairly sound ideas about God and the universe.
p76.014: Adam and Eve began the violet race, the ninth race of Urantia. These people had blue eyes, fair skin, and light-colored hair. Adam and Eve kept up their life by food and by light, and they could see beings invisible to ordinary eyes, such as angels and midwayers. But their children inherited only a little of these special powers, and with each generation their length of life and abilities came closer to those of ordinary people. Adam and his first generation of children did not eat meat; they lived on “⟦Q 76:4.4⟧the fruits of the trees⟦/Q⟧”.
p76.015: The Urantia Book explains that Adam's descendants were more resistant to disease and less shaken by fear, and it finds one reason why humankind today suffers from disease and fear in the fact that Adam's life inheritance did not spread widely. So, according to The Urantia Book, before he died Adam tried to leave his life inheritance through a commission led by Eve, by which children were born to women of various tribes, and these children later became the beginning of the Andites.
p76.017: Some time after the second garden was established, Adam and Eve were told that their repentance had been accepted and that they would be counted worthy to live again after death. This was because their mistake was an error of judgment, not a deliberate rebellion. Thought Adjusters also came to dwell in them, and this gave them great courage for the rest of their lives. Michael (the Creator Son who made and rules our universe) also sent them a message meaning that when he came to Urantia, he would call them from their sleep. Adam did not fully understand what it meant, but he told the people that someday a Son of God would come to this world.
p76.018: Adam lived 530 years and died when his body wore out, and Eve had died nineteen years before him. The two were buried in the middle of the temple. With this, the age of the visible representatives of the universe government on the planet came to an end. But Urantia was not simply an unfortunate world. The darkness and confusion here actually moved Michael's heart, and he chose this world as the stage on which to reveal the love of the heavenly Father.
p76.020: Adam and Eve fell into the sleep of death with a firm faith that they would wake again. And that sleep was not long. On the third day after Adam died, a special resurrection order was given, and Adam and Eve came alive again on the mansion worlds (the worlds where people first wake up and learn after death), together with 1,316 associates who had shared the first Garden with them. They rose quickly and became citizens of Jerusem again, and now they serve as two of the twenty-four counselors who look after Urantia.
p76.021: The story of Adam and Eve is a story of trial, tragedy, and triumph. They made a great contribution to the civilization and progress of humankind, but as their inheritance faded, the high civilization did not last long. The text says, “⟦Q 76:6.4⟧It is the people who make a civilization⟦/Q⟧”. Like Adam and Eve, who repented after their mistake and lived faithfully to the end, we too can build something good again from the place where we fell.
p77.002: On many inhabited planets there are unique beings at a level halfway between humans and angels. They are called midway creatures, or midwayers. At first they seem to have come about by accident, but they are such useful helpers that they are considered a group essential to the care of a planet. Urantia has two groups of midwayers: the primary midwayers, who came about in the days of Dalamatia, and the secondary midwayers, who came about in the days of Adam.
p77.004: The primary midwayers came about on Urantia in a very special way. The corporeal staff of one hundred (the Prince's helpers who had bodies people could see) who came with the Planetary Prince Caligastia had material bodies. When a man and a woman of this staff were united, not in the bodily way but in a supermaterial way, the first midwayer was born. When it became known that these beings were a great help in the Prince's work, each couple of the staff was allowed to produce midwayers, one thousand for each couple, for a total of 50,000.
p77.005: The primary midwayers worked like the Prince's intelligence corps. They traveled far and wide, studied the various races, and did the service the Prince needed to help the people. But when the planetary rebellion broke out, more than four fifths of them were swept into the rebellion. The midwayers who stayed loyal worked to help the Melchizedeks.
p77.007: Half the ancestry of the secondary midwayers came from the Nodites, so the story of the Nodites must be told first. After the rebellion, the sixty members of the staff who followed Nod had children, and The Urantia Book explains that because of the special life circuits that had flowed in the staff's bodies, their offspring were, unexpectedly, superior in body, intellect, and spiritual ability. The Nodites who came about this way are the eighth race of Urantia. The legends of the “⟦Q 77:2.3⟧sons of the gods⟦/Q⟧” and the “⟦Q 77:2.3⟧mighty men of old⟦/Q⟧” in old stories began here too.
p77.008: But the Nodites gradually mixed with other peoples, and their length of life also grew shorter, so that after about ten thousand years they were almost the same as other people. The text says that the old records of the long reigns of ancient Sumerian kings, and of people living nine hundred years, came from memories of the long lives of the early Nodite leaders and from mistaking a moon of twenty-eight days for a year.
p77.010: After Dalamatia sank under the water, the Nodites built a new city called Dilmun. As their numbers grew, their leaders wanted something to bind their people together, and a man named Bablot proposed building a temple with a huge tower. This was the tower of Babel. But people were divided over why the tower was being built. Some wanted to honor the glory of their own people, some wanted to make it the center of Dilmun culture, and a small group wanted to make it a place to repent of their ancestors' rebellion and worship the Father of all.
p77.011: The group that wanted worship lost the vote and left for the south, and the other two groups, unable to settle things by talking, fought each other until almost all of them were killed. Because of pride and quarreling, the tower was never finished.
p77.013: After the fighting over the tower of Babel, the Nodites scattered to many places. This civil war greatly reduced their numbers, and their culture declined for a long time. The scattered Nodites formed four main centers: the Syrian Nodites in the northwest, the Elamite Nodites in the east, the central Nodites at the mouth of the rivers, and the northern Nodites who followed Van and Amadon. The area where the Elamite Nodites lived was later called “⟦Q 77:4.5⟧the land of Nod⟦/Q⟧”, and there the Adamites and Nodites mixed a great deal.
p77.014: The central Nodites later mixed with the Adamites and became the Sumerian people. That is why the Sumerians seem to appear in history suddenly, with a mature culture, from no one knows where. Ancient Sumerian clay tablets still tell of the paradise of Dilmun, where the gods showed humankind the pattern of civilization. The northern Nodites regarded Mount Ararat as a holy mountain and taught that Van had received the seven commandments there.
p77.016: The other half of the ancestry of the secondary midwayers came from Adamson, Adam's firstborn son. Adamson always longed for the northern highlands he had heard about as a child from Van and Amadon, and after the second garden was established, he set out north with twenty-seven others. After searching for more than three years, he met and married a woman named Ratta, who was said to be the last descendant of the Prince's staff.
p77.017: Adamson and Ratta had sixty-seven children, and every fourth child born to them was special and was often invisible to human eyes. Adamson paired these children together, and this is how the secondary midwayers came about. Adamson's center was southeast of the Caspian Sea, and his descendants kept up a high culture for almost seven thousand years, and the seeds of that culture carried on even into later European civilization.
p77.019: Sixteen of Adamson's children were the ancestors of the secondary midwayers. These eight couples each produced 248 midwayers, so that 1,984 secondary midwayers came into being in all. Nothing like this has ever happened on earth, before or since. The ancestors lived and died like ordinary people, but their offspring, the midwayers, are not bound by the limits of a body and are still alive today.
p77.020: After Adamson died, the secondary midwayers lived scattered without order for a long time and caused quite a few problems. Then, while Michael (the Creator Son of our universe, who came to this earth as Jesus) was on earth, they all decided their own future, and the majority who chose loyalty came under the direction of the primary midwayers.
p77.022: At the time of the rebellion, 40,119 of the 50,000 primary midwayers sided with Caligastia, and 873 of the secondary midwayers did not follow Michael. In olden times these rebel midwayers sometimes appeared to human eyes and sometimes influenced the minds of weak people. The evil spirits and devils that ancient writers spoke of usually meant these beings.
p77.023: But now all the rebel midwayers are held prisoner, and they can no longer roam the world doing harm. Especially since Pentecost, when the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all people, no disloyal spirit can enter even the weakest human mind. The text says clearly, “⟦Q 77:7.8⟧Since the day of Pentecost there never again can be such a thing as demoniacal possession.⟦/Q⟧”
p77.025: Today on Urantia the loyal primary and secondary midwayers have joined together and work as the united midwayers, and they number 10,992. They do not eat or sleep and do not have children, but they enjoy human humor and worship and share in human work and play. The secondary midwayers in particular are closer to humans, so they understand people well and feel with them. They work in groups as messengers who carry news, as planetary sentinels who guard the planet, as contact personalities who link humans with heavenly beings, and as helpers who assist the angels.
p77.026: Like the Bible story of an angel opening the prison doors and setting the apostles free, many of the deeds known as the work of angels were actually done by secondary midwayers. They also played a large part in bringing this revelation. But midwayers have nothing at all to do with so-called spiritualism or the activities of mediums.
p77.028: Angels come and go, but the midwayers are the permanent citizens of Urantia who always stay on this planet. They have pledged not to leave the planet until the age of light and life (the time when a planet reaches peace and spiritual perfection) arrives, and their motto is “⟦Q 77:9.3⟧What the United Midwayers undertake, the United Midwayers do.⟦/Q⟧” They are fully grown from the start, yet they keep growing in wisdom and experience, and they are like a treasure house holding the planet's old memories that people have forgotten.
p77.029: The midwayers are our comrades, like older brothers, who have long worked alongside us so that this world may come to peace and good will. When we think of these beings who work faithfully beside us though unseen, we too want to become people who carry out the work given to us, in our own place, to the very end.
p78.002: For almost thirty thousand years the second garden was the cradle of civilization. Adam's descendants who settled in Mesopotamia, the Adamites, sent their offspring out from here to the whole world, and later, after mixing with the Nodites and other peoples, they came to be called the Andites. This paper covers the long history from the time Adam passed on until the violet race finally disappeared from Mesopotamia.
p78.004: When Adam came, people's minds and morals were still at a low level. Thanks to the descendants of Adam and Eve, civilization was greatly hastened, but the world of thirty-five thousand years ago was still mostly without much culture. There were only scattered centers of civilization here and there.
p78.005: At that time the violet race lived in the second garden and in the northern center of the Adamsonites, and at the mouth of the rivers were the Nodites, who kept the culture of the days of Dalamatia. The Andonites were spread across the north, the red man in America, the yellow man in eastern Asia, and the blue man in Europe, and many peoples lived mixed together in India, the Sahara, and around the Mediterranean. The hope of future civilization lay in the second garden in Mesopotamia, and the heavenly observers watched anxiously to see how the descendants of Adam and Eve would live.
p78.006: 2. The Adamites in the Second Garden
p78.007: For thousands of years Adam's descendants worked along the rivers to control the waters, guarded the north, and tried to keep the traditions of the first Eden. They did not forget their mission, and they gladly sent their finest sons and daughters to other peoples as teachers. Because of this, their homeland was sometimes weakened, but it soon recovered.
p78.008: The civilization of the Adamites was far ahead of their surroundings, but it had not grown up slowly by itself; it had been received all at once from Adam. Adam left a superb intellectual and spiritual culture, but he did not develop tools and machines. So after Adam died and the traditions of Eden faded, their culture gradually sank to a level like that of the surrounding peoples. Even so, by about 19,000 B.C. the Adamites had become a great people of four and a half million.
p78.010: For thousands of years the violet race kept the peaceful traditions of Eden. Even as their numbers grew, they did not take land by war but sent their extra people to other peoples as teachers. Some of them went west to the Nile and some east into Asia, but most went north, around the Caspian Sea, and on toward Europe. On their long journeys they mixed with many peoples and lost most of the culture of Eden.
p78.011: By about 15,000 B.C., more descendants of Adam were spread across Europe and central Asia than were in Mesopotamia. In the same period, the Sahara civilization collapsed because of drought, and the Mediterranean civilization collapsed because of floods. This spreading of peoples, together with these changes in climate, set the stage for the beginning of the Andite age.
p78.013: The Andites were a people who came from the mixing of the violet race, the Nodites, and several evolutionary peoples. They arose around Mesopotamia more than twenty-five thousand years ago. The Urantia Book explains that the Andites were a people with outstanding talents in many fields, and that they left traits later shared by the so-called white races. But the early Andites were not Aryans, not white, and neither Occidental nor Oriental.
p78.014: At first the migrations of the Adamites were peaceful. But as they mixed with the warlike Nodites, the Andites became skilled military strategists, and their later migrations became more and more like conquests. The Andites loved adventure and wandering, and their descendants finally went all the way around the globe and discovered even the last remaining continent.
p78.016: Around 15,000 B.C., thanks to a revival among the Sethite priests and a leader named Amosad, a brilliant era came to the second garden again, and soon great waves of Andite civilization spread throughout Eurasia. In Turkestan in central Asia, several languages mixed to form the Aryan mother tongue, and from it many modern languages branched off. The Andites went not only to Europe but also to India, China, and northern Africa.
p78.017: A group of one hundred and thirty-two Andites even set out from Japan in small boats, passed through the islands of the Pacific, and reached South America, where they became the ancestors of the later Inca rulers. Wherever the Andites went, they brought humor and art, adventure, music, crafts, the keeping of animals, and farming, and for a time they also improved the religion and morals of the people there. In this way the culture of Mesopotamia quietly spread to the whole world.
p78.019: Between 8000 and 6000 B.C., in three final great waves, the Andites left Mesopotamia. They were pushed out by the mountain tribes to the east and the people of the plains to the west. Most went to Europe, some went to Iran and Turkestan, toward China, and to Egypt, and only a small group at the mouth of the rivers stayed in their homeland.
p78.020: The Urantia Book explains that the cultural age of the second garden came to an end as the surrounding peoples slowly moved in and mixed with them, followed by the invasion of northern invaders. The center of civilization moved west to the Nile and the Mediterranean islands, and it carried on there for a long time.
p78.022: The people of Mesopotamia were used to the rivers overflowing every year. But starting around 5000 B.C., as the mountains to the north rose higher and snowfall increased, great floods unlike any before came every spring. For almost a thousand years, dozens of cities were abandoned because of these floods.
p78.023: The text says that the story of Noah's flood covering the whole world was made up by Hebrew priests held captive in Babylon as they worked to connect the line of their ancestors. Since life appeared, there has never been a flood that covered the whole earth. But Noah was a real person. He was a winemaker in a riverside town, and he recorded the height of the river every year and urged people to build their houses in the shape of boats, but he was laughed at. Then one year, when heavy rains swept the town away, only Noah's family survived in their houseboat. Through these floods the second garden finally disappeared.
p78.025: The small group left at the mouth of the rivers after the Andites departed were the Sumerians. They were the last Andites of Mesopotamia, keeping the traditions and culture of the Nodites. Even when northern invaders on horseback took over the valley, the Sumerians defended themselves for a long time, thanks to their superior wisdom and weapons, their system of canals, and their united religion. Soon even the invaders came to respect the peace-loving Sumerians as teachers and administrators.
p78.026: But later, each city quarreled that its own god was the greatest, so they could not unite, and the wars between cities never ended. At last, around 2500 B.C., they were badly defeated by northern tribes, and by the time of Hammurabi the Sumerians had been absorbed by the Semites and disappeared from history. But before that, the culture of the Garden had already spread to Asia, Africa, and Europe and became the leaven that grew today's civilization. That good things remained in the world thanks to people who shared what they had and went out to teach gives us something to think about too.
p79.002: Asia is the homeland of humankind. Andon and Fonta, the first humans, were born on this continent, and the Sangik peoples, the races of different colors, also first appeared in Asia. In southwestern Asia the civilizations of Dalamatia, the Nodites, the Adamites, and the Andites rose one after another, and from there the seeds of modern civilization spread to the whole world. This paper tells how the Andites spread to the east, toward India and China.
p79.004: For more than twenty-five thousand years, central Asia was mainly the land of the Andites. From Turkestan they gradually flowed westward into Europe, eastward through Sinkiang and Tibet into China, and southward into India. These early movements were not conquests but peaceful migrations. The Tarim valley in Sinkiang was for a long time the eastern edge of Andite culture, and in those days it was a fertile land with plenty of rain.
p79.005: Starting around 8000 B.C., as central Asia slowly dried up, the Andites moved to the great river valleys, such as the Nile, the Euphrates, the Indus, and the Yellow River. At this time a new class of people, the traders, grew greatly in number, and cities arose where goods were made and bought and sold. As the drought went on, the last great migration of the Andites took place, and the Andites of central Asia almost disappeared. Much later, when the Mongols of Genghis Khan proclaimed “⟦Q 79:1.9⟧one God in heaven⟦/Q⟧”, it was the last echo of that old Andite tradition.
p79.007: India is the only place where all the races of Urantia mixed. From ancient times many peoples gathered in this land, forming the most varied mixture of races in the world. Around 15,000 B.C., as the population grew in Turkestan and Iran, the first large group of Andites entered India and spread along the Indus and Ganges rivers. They sometimes limited marriage to keep their own identity, but in the end most of them mixed with the people there, and thanks to this the whole of India advanced greatly.
p79.008: The Urantia Book explains that it finds the reasons India did not become the center of a civilization leading the world in its geography, closed off by sea on most sides, and in the makeup of its racial mixture there. The Urantia Book also says that the mixing of races in itself is beneficial, because it increases the variety of culture and moves civilization forward.
p79.010: The Andites who entered India mixed with the people there, and the Dravidians came into being. They built the most versatile civilization on earth at that time. The Dravidians were among the first peoples to build cities, and they traded actively by camel caravans and by ships with Sumer in Mesopotamia and as far as the East Indies. They also brought in the alphabet and writing from Sumer.
p79.011: The belief in one God that runs through the religions of India came from the Sethite priests of the second garden. In 16,000 B.C., one hundred Sethite priests entered India and taught many people, but their teachings faded as time went on. Even so, for more than seven thousand years the religious level of the people of India was higher than anywhere else in the world. Dravidian civilization spread throughout India and still survives today in the Deccan region in the south.
p79.013: In the middle of the third millennium B.C., the Aryans came into India from Turkestan. This was the last great migration out of the Andite homelands. The Aryans were few in number, so they did not leave much influence by blood; their influence was mainly in culture and religion. In the Ganges plain, the Aryans and Dravidians mixed and built a high culture.
p79.014: The Aryans created the caste system to keep from mixing with other peoples, and this system survives to this day. But The Urantia Book says that the caste system alone could not preserve their culture. The Brahman priests, the first caste, were the cultural descendants of the Sethite priests, but their teachings came to differ greatly from their forebears', and India fell into superstition and missed its chance for a high civilization. The Urantia Book says that true religion is the very source of the power that leads people to build a civilization where they live as brothers, and it shares the hope that someday a person will arise who will lead all of India to the living God.
p79.016: The story of eastern Asia is mainly the story of the red man and the yellow man. The red man settled first in northeastern Asia and held it for almost one hundred thousand years. More than three hundred thousand years ago, the yellow man entered China along the southern coast, and as he moved gradually northward, a long struggle of more than two hundred thousand years broke out between the two races.
p79.017: At first the red man won, but the yellow man learned early how to live in peace with one another and join forces. The Chinese were the first to realize that there is strength in union. The red tribes, on the other hand, kept fighting among themselves, were finally pushed out, and when the Bering isthmus opened, they crossed over to America. After that, the red man in America lived cut off from the rest of the world for a long time and built his own civilization without the help of the Andites.
p79.019: After driving out the red man, the Chinese established twelve centers of culture and learning along the Yellow River and the Yangtze. Various peoples also lived on the islands of the Pacific, and the ancestors of the Japanese also crossed from the mainland to the islands around this time.
p79.020: There were four reasons the early yellow man moved ahead. The first was the foundation they had inherited. The second was the social strength that came from living together peacefully and growing in population and civilization. The third was the spiritual strength of worshiping the “⟦Q 79:8.4⟧One Truth⟦/Q⟧” taught by Singlangton. The fourth was a geography that protected them, surrounded by mountains and sea. Faith that worshiped truth especially led people to explore eagerly the laws of nature and the possibilities of human beings. From 25,000 to 5000 B.C., the largest high civilization was in China.
p79.022: About fifteen thousand years ago, the Andites crossed the western passes and entered the upper valley of the Yellow River. They were not many, but the northern Chinese who mixed with them became more versatile and moved ahead of the south. The later Andites passed on the economic and educational ways of Mesopotamia, and they also left legends of the beauty of Eden, so that old Chinese legends place “⟦Q 79:7.4⟧the land of the gods⟦/Q⟧” in the west.
p79.023: After 10,000 B.C., the Chinese began building cities, working metals, and making goods. Chinese traders traveled through Turkestan all the way to Mesopotamia, and so the calendars, astronomy, and ways of governing of the two regions came to resemble each other.
p79.025: After taking over all of eastern Asia, the Chinese lived peacefully as farmers for a long time without the threat of foreign enemies. Their love for the family led to ancestor worship, and people more and more put their energy into keeping what they already knew rather than seeking new truth. This is why what had been the world's fastest-advancing civilization came to a standstill. The Urantia Book says that it is wise to gain wisdom from the past but foolish to regard the past as the only source of truth, and it stresses that truth “⟦Q 79:8.8⟧lives always in the present⟦/Q⟧”.
p79.026: But ancestor worship also had great strengths. Because the family was valued above all, property and experience were passed down through the generations, children were well educated, and a strong sense of duty and morality grew. Chinese civilization was second to none in family loyalty, community ethics, and personal morals, and now it is awakening again and beginning new progress. To treasure good traditions while keeping our minds open to new truth: that is the lesson this paper gives us.
